Methodology: Issue
CODARIS treatment
Reason
Catalogue boundary

Separates metrics, telemetry collection, logs, traces, APM platforms, errors, uptime, incident response, profiling and eBPF/runtime observability. OpenTelemetry is instrumentation/collection, not itself a backend database.
A declared taxonomy boundary is more defensible than claiming a finite list of every tool ever created.
Popularity/adoption
Only attach a metric when the source directly measures that named item and population.
Different surveys and telemetry measure different things.
Cross-category overlap
Allow overlap where a tool has multiple genuine roles; label its role in each category.
For example GitHub is a code host while GitHub Actions is CI/CD.
Country data
Do not derive per-tool country usage from overall survey geography.
Overall respondent geography is not a tool-by-country cross-tab.
Gender data
Do not fabricate male/female or other demographic shares by tool.
A direct cross-tab with sample sizes and all source categories is needed.
Lifecycle
Legacy/historical items may be retained for educational context, but inclusion is not a recommendation to adopt.
CODARIS is an educational catalogue, not a procurement ranking.
Sources: Prometheus 77% production; Fluentd 41%; Jaeger 22% among graduated-project respondents.
OpenTelemetry was the second-highest-velocity CNCF project.
Among screened active users, Prometheus exporters 72%, OTel receivers 57%; OTel SDKs 65% for application instrumentation.
